summary:
Nameless Space Game is a 3D PC video game that immerses the player in a space mission to Mars. Its goal is to spark greater interest in space exploration: rather than just reading about such missions, the player gets to experience them firsthand.
The experience consists of two parts. First, the player floats in a space capsule in zero gravity, learning how to navigate. Next, they operate a rover on Mars—modeled after NASA’s Perseverance—collecting rock samples, analyzing their characteristics, and managing the mission’s budget and energy resources.
Take on the challenge of an interactive game where you oversee a space mission, manage limited resources, and see how your decisions shape the outcome.
details:
What does the game do?

Nameless Space Game is a 3D PC video game that immerses players in a mission to Mars. Its goal is to spark greater interest in space missions: instead of simply reading about them, players get to experience one. The experience has two parts. First, players float inside a spacecraft capsule in zero gravity and learn how to move. Then, on Mars, they drive a rover inspired by NASA’s Perseverance, collect rocks, examine their characteristics, and manage the mission’s budget and energy. The game addresses the challenge of creating an interactive experience in which players manage a space mission, work with limited resources, and see how their decisions affect the outcome.

How does it work?

  1. Startup and loading: The game opens with a team-designed title screen and loading screen.
  2. Zero-gravity tutorial: Players begin inside a spacecraft capsule. In a weightless environment, they learn the movement controls before starting the mission.
  3. Mars exploration: Players drive the rover in first-person view across 3D Martian terrain.
  4. Rock collection: The rover collects rocks found across the terrain.
  5. Rock analysis: Each collected rock displays its characteristics in an information panel based on real data about Martian meteorites.
  6. Resource management: Throughout the mission, dashboards display the available budget and energy. Players must manage both to keep exploring. A soundtrack and rover movement sounds accompany the experience.

Benefits and Impact

Social: Makes space exploration more accessible to people with no prior exposure to the subject and may inspire interest in science and engineering careers, especially among young people.

Environmental: By managing the rover’s energy, players practice using limited resources responsibly. Exploring a planet with no visible life also encourages appreciation of Earth’s conditions.

Technological: Demonstrates that a four-person team can create a 3D game in two days by combining Unity, Blender, and artificial intelligence.

Methodology and Tools

  • Unity: Game engine used for environments, player and rover movement, first-person camera, and mission logic.
  • Unity UI Toolkit: User Interface for the game.
  • Claude with an MCP extension for Blender: Assistance with generating models and textures.
  • Claude: Generation of terrrain of the game based on HiRISE temperature map.
  • Inkscape: Layout and design of visual elements.
  • GitHub: Team collaboration: each member developed one part and uploaded it to the repository.
  • Language: C#
  • Platform: PC

Project Management

Project Location: Cajamarca, Perú

Our Institution: Universidad Nacional de Cajamarca

Relevance to NASA's mission

  • Mars exploration: Players do what the Perseverance rover does: travel across Mars, collect rocks, and study them.
  • Use of NASA open resources: The game was built using information about Martian meteorites, Mars heat maps, space exploration videos, and NASA’s official 3D rover model.
  • Inspiration and public outreach: NASA aims to inspire new generations and make science more accessible to the public. The game pursues the same goal in a format that appeals to young people.
  • Responding to the challenge: Players manage a mission with limited resources (budget and energy) and see how their decisions affect what they can accomplish.

Conclusions and Future Improvements

In two days, a four-person team built a 3D game that takes players from a spacecraft capsule in zero gravity to the surface of Mars. The project shows that space exploration can be shared in an engaging way using accessible tools and NASA open data.

Lessons learned

  • Dividing the work by area and combining it through GitHub made parallel development possible.
  • AI accelerated 3D modeling and audio creation, leaving more time to focus on gameplay.
  • Simplifying the rover model compared with NASA’s original was necessary for good performance.
  • Planning interface designs in Inkscape before building them in Unity helped organize the UI work.

Potential improvements

  • Add more types of rocks and expand the scientific information provided for each one.
  • Introduce events that affect energy, such as dust storms or the day-night cycle.
  • Add more mission stages, including launch, the journey to Mars, and landing.
  • Include a pre-mission design phase in which players choose the rover’s instruments based on their budget.
  • Test the game with students and measure whether it increases their interest in space missions.
